sections.title: From "ever" to "this once"
sections.content: *már* tells you an experience exists somewhere in your past, without pinning it to a moment. *először* ("for the first time") does the opposite: it takes you back to one specific occasion and marks it as the first of its kind — a normal narrated past-tense event, exactly like Unit 1's storytelling, except now flagged as a first. *életemben először* ("for the first time in my life") makes the claim even bigger, and *most először* ("this time, for the first time") ties it to the here and now.

sections.title: először, in context
rows: This is the first time I've been to Japan.
For the first time in my life, I tried surfing.
At first I didn't like it, then I grew to love it.

sections.title: One specific first time, not a general experience

items.english: Last summer I flew for the first time in my life.

items.spanish: Amikor először kipróbáltam a szörfözést, mindenki nevetett rajtam.
items.english: When I tried surfing for the first time, everyone laughed at me.

sections.content: *Már jártam Japánban* and *Most jártam először Japánban* sound similar but answer different questions: *már* answers "has this ever happened to you?", *először* tells the story of one particular occasion. Don't combine them in the same clause — *Már jártam először Japánban* doesn't make sense, because *először* already picks out one specific time, and *már* deliberately avoids doing that.
